{{Short description|11th season of a nationwide round-robin club competition in New Zealand football}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2019}}
{{Use New Zealand English|date=April 2019}}
The '''1980 New Zealand National Soccer League''' was the 11th season of a nationwide [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] club competition in [[New Zealand]] football. [[Mount Wellington (soccer)|Mount Wellington]] became the first club to win back-to-back titles and also the first club to win the league four times, though their winning margin was significantly smaller than in 1979.

==Promotion and relegation==
Promotion was automatic, with the three lowest placed sides in the 1979 league ([[Manawatu United]], [[Courier Rangers]], and [[Eastern Suburbs AFC|Eastern Suburbs]]) replaced by the winners of the northern, central, and southern leagues ([[Hamilton (soccer)|Hamilton]], [[Gisborne City]], and [[Christchurch Rangers|Rangers]] respectively).<ref name="rsssf80">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesn/nz80.html|title = New Zealand 1980}}</ref>

==Team performance==
Mount Wellington's win may have been only bo four points (down from the 14 points in [[1979 New Zealand National Soccer League|1979]]), but it was still a heavy victory. No other team looked like serious contenders. The Mount set several league records, notably a 9–1 win over [[Stop Out]] in Lower Hutt which was the league's biggest winning margin to that time, and also an unbeaten run of 13 matches which beat the league's previous record. [[Gisborne City]]'s first season in the top flight since 1976 was successful, and an undefeated season at home enabled them to finish second overall. [[Manurewa (soccer)|Manurewa]] finished third, and could have finished higher if its home record had been as good as its form on the road. [[Wellington Diamond United]] improved from a poor start to the season which saw them briefly at the foot of the table, and they managed to pull themselves up to fourth.<ref name="Hilton98">Hilton (1991), p. 98</ref>

Hanimex [[North Shore United]] and the newly promoted [[Dunedin City AFC|Dunedin City]] rounded out the top half of the table. A poor start to the season by Shore and a mid-season slump from the southerners hindered the two sides from finishing higher up the table. [[Christchurch United]] had a poor season by their high standards, finishing in seventh. Their season started strongly with five wins on the trot, but their luck changed dramatically and they only won one of their last 14 games. [[Hamilton (soccer)|Hamilton]]'s second spell as a national league side started with them finishing in a comfortable if not brilliant position in eighth. Their home form was good, but they were let down by their away record, and the defence which had only let in four goals in their 1979 regional season found the national league an entirely different proposition.<ref name="Hilton989">Hilton (1991), p. 98-99</ref>

[[Christchurch Rangers|Rangers']] debut season was forgettable, though they did finish above the drop zone. They never fully recovered from losing five of their first seven games, and it was only a good spell in the middle of the season which enabled them to retain their league status. The three teams which did go down included two founding members of the league, [[Stop Out]] and [[Blockhouse Bay (soccer)|Blockhouse Bay]]. Stop Out's season was poor but they did have one thing for which it was memorable — the debut of a young [[Wynton Rufer]], later to make his mark both in New Zealand and overseas. Blockhouse Bay had been inaugural champions of the league in [[1970 New Zealand National Soccer League|1970]], but a decade on their team was not of the same standard, and they never recovered from 10 defeats in their first 12 matches. Last-placed [[Nelson United]] also had a horror start to the season, though a mid-season revival did raise supporters' hopes of survival. It was not to be, however, and the Nelson side slumped to four losses in their last four games.<ref name="Hilton989"/>
